rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿArḍ means perishable worldly goods, as in the worldly gain people seek and the transient goods they take.
rows.anchor: تريدون عرض الدنيا اي ما لا يبقى قال تعالى في سورة الاعراف ياخذون عرض هذا الادنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUrḍa means a cause or pretext, so God is not to be made an excuse for oaths.
rows.anchor: ولا تجعلوا الله عرضة لايمانكم يعني علة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿrūf here means a loan or allowance; the same sense occurs in the passage about charitable confidential counsel.
rows.anchor: ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف يعني بالقرض نظيرها فيها لا خير في كثير من نجواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿrūf can describe a woman adorning herself after her waiting period ends.
rows.anchor: المعروف ان تتزين المرأة بعد انقضاء عدتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a marriage proposal, al-maʿrūf means a kindly promise; the text compares this to gracious speech and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: الا ان تقولوا قولا معروفا يعني عدة حسنة كقوله سبحانه فيها قول معروف ومغفرة خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿrūf can mean maintenance or a gift set according to the man's means.
rows.anchor: وللمطلقات متاع بالمعروف حقا على المتقين اي على قدر ميسور الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿazīz can mean impregnable or mighty; Dāmghānī applies this sense to the taunt in 44:49 and parallel descriptions of strength.
rows.anchor: في سورة الدخان ذق انك انت العزيز الكريم نزلت في ابي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāmghānī says the taunt calling the condemned man mighty and noble was revealed concerning Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: ذق انك انت العزيز الكريم نزلت في ابي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿazīz can mean great in status or kingly might; the source applies the same sense to Hūd, Pharaoh, and the queen of Sheba.
rows.anchor: فبعزتك لاغوينهم يعني فبعظمتك كقوله تعالى في سورة هود وما انت علينا بعزيز يعني بعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIzza means proud zeal or haughtiness, paired here with opposition.
rows.anchor: بل الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق يعني في حمية واختلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When something is ʿazīz upon the Prophet, it is hard or distressing for him.
rows.anchor: عزيز عليه ما عنتم يعني شديدا يشق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-ʿazzaznā means that God strengthened the two messengers by sending a third.
rows.anchor: فعززنا بثالث يعني قويناهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm can mean intention or purpose: once the Prophet resolves, he is to trust in God.
rows.anchor: فإذا عزمت فتوكل على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm can mean patience or steadfast resolve, as in the command to be patient like the resolute messengers.
rows.anchor: ولم نجد له عزما يعني صبرا كقوله تعالى في سورة الاحقاف فاصبر كما صبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resolute messengers are Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: العزم من الرسل وهم خمسة من الانبياء نوح وابراهيم وموسى وعيسى ومحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittakhadhat can mean that Mary drew or spread a screen apart from her family.
rows.anchor: اتخذت أرخت . كقوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittakhadha can mean to believe or affirm a covenant with God that there is no deity but Him.
rows.anchor: اتخذ يعني اعتقد قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ākhira can mean the Resurrection or life after death; in 92:13 it is paired with the present world.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : الآخرة بمعنى القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ākhira can refer specifically to Paradise, where the person who bought sorcery has no share.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الآخرة الجنة خاصة فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ākhira can refer specifically to Hell, contrasted here with the mercy and hope associated with Paradise.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الآخرة يعني النار قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ākhira can mean the last or most recent one: the latest prior religious community, or the later of two promised punishments.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الآخرة يعني الأخيرة . قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ākhira can mean the grave, where the believers are questioned by Munkar and Nakīr.
rows.anchor: الخامس : الآخرة يعني القبر . قوله تعالى في سورة إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A brother may be a full sibling; the source illustrates this kinship with Adam's sons and inheritance verses.
rows.anchor: الأخ يعني من أبيه وأمه . فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A brother can mean a fellow tribesman, as Hūd was a brother to ʿĀd without being their sibling or sharing their religion.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الأخ من القبيلة وليس من أبيه وأمه ولا على دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brothers can be allies in disbelief: the verse's brothers are devils who lead disbelievers further astray.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الأخ في الدين والولاية في الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brothers can be united by the religion and alliance of Islam.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الأخ في دين الإسلام والولاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brothers can mean people joined by love and affection, as Paradise's inhabitants sit facing one another.
rows.anchor: ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل إخوانا على سرر متقابلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brother can mean a companion or associate, as in the speaker's story of the man with ninety-nine ewes.
rows.anchor: إن هذا أخي له تسع وتسعون نعجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sister can mean a group like or resembling the one before it; each nation curses its counterpart.
rows.anchor: السابع : الأخ الشبه قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhinat means heard and obeyed; the source compares the sky's hearing to the addressees saying they heard.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : الإذن بمعنى السماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhina can mean to call out or announce, as a caller addresses the people between Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: الثاني : إذن بمعنى نادى , قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's permission can mean His will; the author gives the same sense for examples in Yūnus and Āl ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الإذن في الشيء من الله تعالى بمعنى الإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions of Moses can mean his people or nation.
rows.anchor: قال اصحاب موسى انا لمدركون يعني قومه وامته ونحوه كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṣāḥib can mean a travel companion or fellow traveler.
rows.anchor: والصاحب بالجنب يعني الرفيق في السفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣāḥib can refer to the Prophet: the verse denies that your prophet is mad.
rows.anchor: وما صاحبكم بمجنون يعني وما نبيكم بمجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣāḥib can mean a brother, as in the exchange between the two men in the garden narrative.
rows.anchor: قال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره يعني لاخيه مثلها فيها قال له صاحبه يعني اخاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāḥiba can mean a wife or spouse.
rows.anchor: وصاحبنه واخيه يعني زوجته كقوله تعالى في سورة الانعام ولم تكن له صاحبة يعني زوجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions of Hell are its keepers, the angels assigned to guard it.
rows.anchor: وما جعلنا اصحاب النار الا ملائكة يعني خزنة النار ولا نظير له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions who call a person to guidance can mean that person's parents.
rows.anchor: له اصحاب يدعونه الى الهدى يعني الابوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaṣuddūn can mean turning away or avoiding someone.
rows.anchor: رأيت المنافقين يصدون عنك صدودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaṣuddūn can mean preventing people from believing in God.
rows.anchor: إن الذين كفروا ويصدون عن سبيل الله اي يمنعون الناس عن الايمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaṣiddūn can mean laughing.
rows.anchor: إذا قومك منه يصدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣaddā means turning one's face toward someone.
rows.anchor: فأنت له تصدى تقبل بوجهك عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣadʿ can mean a split or fissure in the earth.
rows.anchor: والارض ذات الصدع اي النبات وقيل الشق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reported sense of ṣadʿ is vegetation growing from the earth.
rows.anchor: الصدع الشق وقيل النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-iṣdaʿ means to make the commanded message manifest.
rows.anchor: فاصدع بما تؤمر يقول اظهره

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies God's rope as the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود حبل الله القرآن الثالث الحبل الاسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥabl can mean Islam.
rows.anchor: الثالث الحبل الاسلام قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران الا بحبل من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥabl can mean a literal rope made of palm fiber.
rows.anchor: في جيدها حبل من مسد يعني رسنا من ليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā can mean up to or until a stated endpoint.
rows.anchor: انا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر إلى قوله حتى مطلع الفجر يعني إلى مطلع الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā can mean when or once an event has occurred, as when the messengers despaired of their people believing.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل يعني فلما استيأس الرسل من ايمان قومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā can mark the time or condition that ends an ongoing action, as fighting continues until tribute is paid.
rows.anchor: قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله إلى قوله حتى يعطوا الجزية يقول سبحانه قاتلوهم أبدا حتى يقروا الجزية هذا وقت لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥijāb can mean a mountain, the barrier behind which the sun disappeared.
rows.anchor: حتى توارت بالحجاب يعني بالجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥijāb can mean a physical screen or covering.
rows.anchor: فسألوهن من وراء حجاب يعني الساتر كقوله تعالى في سورة مريم فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijāb can mean an impediment that prevents a person from seeing God.
rows.anchor: أو من وراء حجاب كقوله تعالى في سورة المطففين كلا إنهم عن ربهم يومئذ لمحجوبون بآفة مانعة لهم من الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥijāb can mean a wall separating two groups.
rows.anchor: وبينهما حجاب أي سور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ḥ-j-j can mean disputing or arguing.
rows.anchor: قل أتحاجوننا في الله وهو ربنا وربكم أي تخاصموننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥujja can mean a decisive or conclusive proof.
rows.anchor: فلله الحجة البالغة فلو شاء لهداكم أجمعين أي لله الحجة الوثيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stones used as Hell's fuel can mean sulfur stones.
rows.anchor: وقودها الناس والحجارة حجارة الكبريت

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the stones are sulfur, which God made an admonition as He willed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود حجارة من كبريت جعلها الله تعالى عبرة كما شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥajar can mean an ordinary stone, such as the stone Moses struck with his staff.
rows.anchor: أن اضرب بعصاك الحجر ومثلها فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijāra can mean baked clay or brick; the source explains sijjīl as clay and cites parallel descriptions.
rows.anchor: ترميهم بحجارة من سجيل يعني من طين مثلها في سورة هود وامطرنا عليهم حجارة من سجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijr can mean reason or intellect.
rows.anchor: هل في ذلك قسم لذي حجر أي لذي عقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijr can mean something forbidden or prohibited.
rows.anchor: ويقولون حجرا محجورا يعني حراما محرما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥijr can refer to the settlement of the people of Ṣāliḥ.
rows.anchor: ولقد كذب أصحاب الحجر المرسلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥujūr can mean homes: the stepdaughters are in the men's houses or care.
rows.anchor: وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم من نسائكم يعني في بيوتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥadīth can mean a report or piece of news.
rows.anchor: أتحدثونهم بما فتح الله عليكم أي تخبرونهم بما فتح الله عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥadīth can mean speech or a statement.
rows.anchor: ومن أصدق من الله حديثا يعني قولا كقوله تعالى في سورة التحريم وإذ أسر النبي إلى بعض أزواجه حديثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥadīth can mean the Qurʾān, the scripture comparable to God's book.
rows.anchor: فليأتوا بحديث مثله يعني بقرآن مثله كقوله تعالى في سورة المرسلات فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best ḥadīth can mean the best stories or narratives.
rows.anchor: الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا يعني أحسن القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥādīth can mean cautionary examples or tales told about a people who have disappeared.
rows.anchor: وجعلناهم أحاديث يعني عبرا بعدهم يتحدث بها من بعدهم لأنه لم يبق منهم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥadīd can describe sharp or piercing sight.
rows.anchor: فبصرك اليوم حديد يعني حادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥadīd can mean iron as a material.
rows.anchor: وأنزلنا الحديد فيه بأس شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakan and sakīna mean tranquility or reassurance for the heart.
rows.anchor: السكن والسكينة بمعنى الطمأنينة قوله تعالى في سورة براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sakīna placed in the Ark is described as an object like a cat's head with two wings.
rows.anchor: آية ملكه أن يأتيكم التابوت في سكينة من ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulṭān can mean proof or argument; the source says this is the meaning in all Qurʾānic mentions concerning Moses.
rows.anchor: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulṭān can mean dominion or power to compel, as Satan says he had no power to force people into disbelief.
rows.anchor: ما كان لي عليكم من سلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salaf can mean an example or admonition for those who come afterward.
rows.anchor: فجعلناهم سلفا " أي عظة وعبرة لمن يأتي بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salaf can mean what has passed or preceded in the earlier religious dispensation.
rows.anchor: الثاني : سلف أي ما تقدم قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aslaka can mean to put or insert something into a place.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : أسلك يعني أدخل قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salaka can mean to place or set something, as God places a guard before and behind the messenger.
rows.anchor: الثاني : السلك بمعنى الجعل قوله تعالى في سورة الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaslukhu can mean to subject someone to a harsh, arduous punishment.
rows.anchor: الثالث : السلك التكليف قوله تعالى في سورة الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naslukuhu can mean to leave or lodge something in the hearts of the guilty.
rows.anchor: الرابع : السلك الترك قوله تعالى في سورة الحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islām can mean sincerity or wholehearted devotion.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : الإسلام يعني الإخلاص قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taste can mean to receive or experience a favor, such as mercy or well-being from God.
rows.anchor: الذوق الإنالة قوله تعالى في سورة يس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taste can mean to experience the consequence or penalty of one's conduct.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الذوق الوجود قوله تعالى في سورة الطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhāqa can mean to eat, as Adam and his wife ate from the tree.
rows.anchor: فلما ذاقا الشجرة بدت لهما سوآتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taste can mean to punish; God made the town taste hunger and fear and will make people taste a nearer punishment.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الذوق العذاب قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taste can mean to witness or experience something directly, as every soul experiences death.
rows.anchor: الخامس : الذوق المعاينة قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾā can mean to know or teach; the Prophet judges by what God has made known to him.
rows.anchor: يرى يعلم قوله تعالى في سورة سبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾā can mean seeing and directly witnessing what is before one's eyes.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الرؤية بمعنى المشاهدة والمعاينة قوله تعالى في سورة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A-lam tara can mean consider or look at what people are doing, rather than simply witness an event.
rows.anchor: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يؤمنون بالجبت والطاغوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiyāna can mean betraying a trust; the source applies it to the person who stole a coat of mail.
rows.anchor: الخيانة التي تكون ضد الأمانة فيخون بها قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāmghānī says the verse was revealed about Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq, who had stolen an iron coat of mail in his possession.
rows.anchor: نزلت في طعمة بن أبيرق خان في درع من حديد كانت عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiyāna can mean breach of a treaty; the group in question had planned to kill the Prophet and his companions.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الخيانة يعني نقض العهد قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wife's betrayal can mean religious disloyalty: Noah's and Lot's wives were unbelievers, not adulteresses.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الخيانة بمعنى الخلاف في الدين قوله سبحانه وتعالى في سورة التحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the account of Badr's captives, treachery means apostasy, and their earlier betrayal of God means they had disbelieved.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiyāna can mean disloyalty to the faith; the source identifies the hypocritical Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq as an example.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiyāna can mean adultery or sexual misconduct.
rows.anchor: الخامس : الخيانة يعني الزنا قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr can mean wealth, as in the bequest verse and several commands to spend one's good or property.
rows.anchor: الخير بمعنى المال قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr can mean faith: if God knew faith in the captives, He would have enabled them to hear.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الخير يعني الإيمان قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr can mean Islam; in the phrase “denying good,” the source refers to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra preventing his nephew from converting.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الخير يعني الإسلام قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭayyibāt can mean lawful things, including the crops and livestock the pre-Islamic Arabs used.
rows.anchor: الطيبات الحلال وما كان لاهل الجاهلية من مواشي الحرث والانعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭayyibāt can refer to manna and quails provided to the Israelites.
rows.anchor: كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم كقوله سبحانه في سورة يونس ولقد بوأنا بني إسرائيل

words: لَا تُحَرِّمُوا۟ طَيِّبَٰتِ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-ṭayyibāt means food, clothing, and sexual relations that some Companions had chosen to renounce.
rows.anchor: لا تحرموا طيبات ما احل الله لكم يعني الطعام واللباس والجماع

words: لَا تُحَرِّمُوا۟ طَيِّبَٰتِ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition against renouncing these lawful pleasures is said to have been revealed about a group of Companions, including ʿAlī and ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn.
rows.anchor: نزلت في جماعة من اصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم علي بن ابي طالب وعثمان بن مظعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭayyibāt can mean meat, fats, and animals with claws, which had been forbidden in the Torah but were once lawful.
rows.anchor: الرابع الطيبات اللحوم والشحوم وكل ذي ظفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭayyibāt can mean animals slaughtered as food and made lawful for people.
rows.anchor: يسالونك ماذا احل لهم قل احل لكم الطيبات يعني الذبائح طيبة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭayyibāt can mean the lawful booty captured at Badr.
rows.anchor: فكلوا مما غنمتم حلالا طيبا يعني يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings' good provisions include grains, honey, ghee, and other choice foods, which are better than the provisions of animals and birds.
rows.anchor: ورزقناهم من الطيبات يعني جميع رزق بني ادم الحب والعسل والسمن ونحوه من اطيب الطعام وجعل رزقهم اطيب من رزق الدواب والطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭayyibāt can mean good or beautiful speech associated with good men and women.
rows.anchor: الطيبات للطيبين من الرجال والنساء يعني الحسني الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the contrast between khabīth and ṭayyib, the terms mean forbidden and lawful.
rows.anchor: قل لا يستوي الخبيث والطيب يعني الحلال والحرام
